name: clearAllStatistics
description: Deletes the heartbeats and uptime statistics of EVERY monitor, and restarts the active ones; monitors and settings are kept. Cannot be undone. Only when the user explicitly asks to reset all history: confirm with them first, then pass confirm: true. For one monitor use clearMonitorHeartbeats.

arguments.name: confirm
arguments.desc: Must be true: confirms that the user asked to delete every monitor's history

name: clearMonitorEvents
description: Empties a monitor's event list, the status changes listHeartbeats returns with important: true: every heartbeat's message is blanked and none counts as a status change any more. The heartbeats and the uptime statistics are kept. Cannot be undone.

arguments.name: monitorID
arguments.desc: The monitor whose events to clear. Find IDs with listMonitors.

name: clearMonitorHeartbeats
description: Deletes all of one monitor's heartbeats and uptime statistics, so its history and uptime start again from the next check; an active monitor is restarted. The monitor and its settings are kept. Cannot be undone. To clear only its event list, use clearMonitorEvents; for every monitor at once, clearAllStatistics.

arguments.name: monitorID
arguments.desc: The monitor whose history to delete. Find IDs with listMonitors.

name: createAPIKey
description: Creates an API key and returns it. It is sent as the password of HTTP basic auth, with any username. This is the only time the key can be read, and it stays in this conversation's transcript, so give it to the user to store and do not repeat it. Note: once any key exists, Uptime Kuma's /metrics endpoint takes API keys instead of the admin username and password, so a Prometheus scraper still using those must switch.

arguments.name: name
arguments.desc: What the key is for, e.g. "prometheus"

arguments.name: expires
arguments.desc: When it stops working, in the server's local time: "YYYY-MM-DD" (end of that day) or "YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm". Omit for never.

name: createDockerHost
description: Creates a Docker daemon connection; docker monitors take the returned ID in their docker_host field. Pass dockerType "socket" with a socket path, or "tcp" with a URL such as http://host:2375 (for example a docker-socket-proxy). The connection is saved without being checked, so call testDockerHost first. To change one use updateDockerHost.

arguments.name: name
arguments.desc: Human-readable name for this docker host

arguments.name: dockerType
arguments.desc: "socket" for a unix socket path, "tcp" for an HTTP/HTTPS URL

arguments.name: dockerDaemon
arguments.desc: Unix socket path (e.g. /var/run/docker.sock) when dockerType=socket, or TCP URL (e.g. http://docker-proxy:2375) when dockerType=tcp

name: createIncident
description: Posts an incident banner on a status page, for example "API degraded". It shows on the page at once, pinned and active, alongside any other active incidents. Follow up with updateIncident as things change, and resolveIncident when it is over.

arguments.name: slug
arguments.desc: The status page slug. Find slugs with listStatusPages.

arguments.name: title
arguments.desc: Headline of the banner

arguments.name: content
arguments.desc: Body of the banner, in Markdown

arguments.name: style
arguments.desc: Banner color (default: primary). primary, info, warning, danger, light or dark

name: createMaintenanceWindow
description: Schedules a new maintenance window: while it is in effect the monitors in monitorIDs show MAINTENANCE instead of DOWN and do not alert. A window without monitorIDs suppresses nothing. strategy sets the schedule; "manual" makes a window you switch on and off with setMaintenanceWindowActive. To stop one monitor's checks outright use setMonitorActive.

arguments.name: title
arguments.desc: Title of the maintenance window

arguments.name: strategy
arguments.desc: Scheduling strategy: single=one-time, recurring-interval=every N days, recurring-weekday=specific weekdays, recurring-day-of-month=specific dates, cron=starts on a cron expression and lasts durationMinutes, manual=on whenever active

arguments.name: active
arguments.desc: Whether the window is active (default: true). For a manual window, active means in maintenance right now.

arguments.name: description
arguments.desc: Description or reason for the maintenance

arguments.name: timezone
arguments.desc: Timezone the dates and times are in (e.g. "America/New_York", "UTC"). Omit to follow the server timezone.

arguments.name: dateRange
arguments.desc: [start, end] as local times in the window's timezone, e.g. ["2026-10-08T10:00", "2026-10-08T12:00"]. Required for single; optional bounds for recurring strategies; ignored for manual.

arguments.name: timeRange
arguments.desc: Daily [{hours, minutes}, {hours, minutes}] start and end. Required for the recurring-* strategies, ignored otherwise.

arguments.name: weekdays
arguments.desc: Days of week (0=Sunday … 6=Saturday) for recurring-weekday strategy

arguments.name: daysOfMonth
arguments.desc: Days of month (1-31) for recurring-day-of-month strategy

arguments.name: intervalDay
arguments.desc: Interval in days for recurring-interval strategy

arguments.name: cron
arguments.desc: Cron expression for when the window starts, e.g. "30 3 * * *" (03:30 daily), for the cron strategy

arguments.name: durationMinutes
arguments.desc: How long each window lasts, in minutes, for the cron strategy

arguments.name: monitorIDs
arguments.desc: IDs of the monitors this window suppresses. A window with no monitors suppresses nothing. On update this REPLACES the current list; pass [] to detach all.

arguments.name: statusPageSlugs
arguments.desc: Slugs of the status pages that announce this window while it is in effect. On update this REPLACES the current list; pass [] to remove it from all. Find slugs with listStatusPages.

name: createMonitor
description: Creates a new monitor from a name, a type and the fields that type requires. Choose the type with listMonitorTypes, preferring one made for the service over a generic port check, then call getMonitorTypeFields for its required and optional fields, their defaults and where each is passed. A create that lacks a required field is refused rather than saved as a monitor that fails every check. A push monitor's generated token and ping URL are returned. To change an existing monitor use updateMonitor.

arguments.name: name
arguments.desc: Display name for the monitor

arguments.name: type
arguments.desc: Monitor type (e.g. http, port, ping, dns, push, keyword). Use listMonitorTypes for all options.

arguments.name: description
arguments.desc: Free-text description shown on the monitor page

arguments.name: active
arguments.desc: Whether the monitor starts checking immediately (default: true). Pass false to create it paused.

arguments.name: resendInterval
arguments.desc: Resend notification every N checks while down (0 = disabled, the default)

arguments.name: timeout
arguments.desc: Request timeout in seconds. Omit for the type's default, which getMonitorTypeFields gives. Avoid 0: Uptime Kuma turns a stored 0 into a timeout of about 13 hours, so the monitor never reports DOWN.

arguments.name: jsonPath
arguments.desc: JSONata expression for json-query monitors. Must resolve to a primitive.

arguments.name: jsonPathOperator
arguments.desc: Comparison operator for json-query monitors. UP while value <operator> expectedValue.

arguments.name: expectedValue
arguments.desc: Threshold the json-query result is compared against. Stored as a string.

arguments.name: pushToken
arguments.desc: Push token for push monitors — the secret in the ping URL. Omit and one is generated and returned.

arguments.name: url
arguments.desc: URL to check (http, keyword, json-query and other URL-based types)

arguments.name: hostname
arguments.desc: Hostname or IP address to check (port, ping, dns and most non-HTTP types)

arguments.name: port
arguments.desc: Port number (port, and other types that take one)

arguments.name: interval
arguments.desc: Check interval in seconds (default: 60, or 300 for ntp; min: 1)

arguments.name: retryInterval
arguments.desc: Retry interval in seconds when monitor is down (default: the interval, min: 1)

arguments.name: maxretries
arguments.desc: Max retries before marking as down (default: 0)

arguments.name: notificationIDList
arguments.desc: Map of notification IDs to enable (e.g. {"1": true, "3": true})

arguments.name: tags
arguments.desc: Tags to assign to the monitor

arguments.name: keyword
arguments.desc: Keyword to search for (keyword monitor type)

arguments.name: invertKeyword
arguments.desc: Invert keyword match

arguments.name: method
arguments.desc: HTTP method (GET, POST, etc.) for http type

arguments.name: body
arguments.desc: HTTP request body

arguments.name: headers
arguments.desc: HTTP headers as JSON string

arguments.name: accepted_statuscodes
arguments.desc: Accepted HTTP status codes (e.g. ["200-299"])

arguments.name: ignoreTls
arguments.desc: Ignore TLS/SSL errors

arguments.name: maxredirects
arguments.desc: Max HTTP redirects (default: 10)

arguments.name: upsideDown
arguments.desc: Invert status — treat up as down

arguments.name: expiryNotification
arguments.desc: Notify before the TLS certificate expires (http, keyword, json-query, globalping)

arguments.name: domainExpiryNotification
arguments.desc: Notify before the domain registration expires. Needs Uptime Kuma 2.1 or later.

arguments.name: parent
arguments.desc: Parent group monitor ID

arguments.name: docker_container
arguments.desc: Docker container name (required for docker type)

arguments.name: docker_host
arguments.desc: Docker host ID (required for docker type). Use listDockerHosts to find available IDs.

arguments.name: dns_resolve_server
arguments.desc: DNS server to use for resolution (required for dns type, default: 1.1.1.1)

arguments.name: dns_resolve_type
arguments.desc: DNS record type to query (dns and globalping; default: A)

arguments.name: databaseConnectionString
arguments.desc: Connection string for the database monitor types. A credential.

arguments.name: databaseQuery
arguments.desc: Query a database monitor runs. Omit for the type's default.

arguments.name: databasePassword
arguments.desc: Password for mysql monitors, if not in the connection string. A credential.

arguments.name: radiusPassword
arguments.desc: The RADIUS password (radius). A credential.

arguments.name: typeFields
arguments.desc: Type-specific fields, e.g. {"mqttTopic": "sensors/#"} for mqtt or {"bearer_token": "…"} for HTTP with auth. getMonitorTypeFields names them for a type; an unknown name is refused. getMonitor returns them at the top level.

name: createNotification
description: Creates a notification channel from a name, a type and that type's config fields. Choose the type with listNotificationTypes, then call getNotificationTypeFields for its field names: both are case-sensitive. A create that lacks a documented required field is refused rather than saved as a channel that never sends. Attach the channel with notificationIDList on createMonitor / updateMonitor, or pass applyExisting. A repeat call creates a second channel; to change one use updateNotification.

arguments.name: name
arguments.desc: Human-readable name for this notification channel

arguments.name: type
arguments.desc: Notification type, e.g. slack, smtp, PagerDuty. Use listNotificationTypes for all options.

arguments.name: isDefault
arguments.desc: Enable by default for new monitors

arguments.name: applyExisting
arguments.desc: Attach this channel to every existing monitor now

arguments.name: config
arguments.desc: The fields of this notification type, e.g. {"slackwebhookURL": "https://hooks.slack.com/…"} for slack. Call getNotificationTypeFields for the names.

name: createProxy
description: Adds an HTTP or SOCKS proxy. Monitors use it once their proxyId is set to its ID (createMonitor / updateMonitor), or all at once with applyExisting. Pass username and password for a proxy that needs them.

arguments.name: protocol
arguments.desc: Proxy protocol: http, https, socks, socks5, socks5h, socks4

arguments.name: host
arguments.desc: Proxy host name or IP address

arguments.name: port
arguments.desc: Proxy port

arguments.name: username
arguments.desc: For a proxy that needs a login

arguments.name: password
arguments.desc: For a proxy that needs a login. A credential.

arguments.name: default
arguments.desc: Make it the proxy the web UI preselects for new monitors; the previous default stops being one

arguments.name: applyExisting
arguments.desc: Also route every existing monitor through this proxy now. One-off: it is not stored.

arguments.name: includeSecrets
arguments.desc: Return credentials in full instead of "***"; they then stay in the transcript. Default: false, or UPTIME_KUMA_INCLUDE_SECRETS.

name: createRemoteBrowser
description: Adds a remote browser. Real-browser monitors use it once their remote_browser field is set to its ID. Check the URL first with testRemoteBrowser.

arguments.name: name
arguments.desc: A name to tell it apart

arguments.name: url
arguments.desc: WebSocket endpoint, e.g. ws://browserless:3000?token=…

arguments.name: includeSecrets
arguments.desc: Return credentials in full instead of "***"; they then stay in the transcript. Default: false, or UPTIME_KUMA_INCLUDE_SECRETS.

name: createStatusPage
description: Creates an empty status page from a title and a slug (lowercase letters, digits and dashes only). It has no groups or monitors yet: add them, and the description and theme, with updateStatusPage.

arguments.name: title
arguments.desc: Display title of the status page

arguments.name: slug
arguments.desc: URL slug (lowercase letters, digits, and dashes only)

name: createTag
description: Creates a tag with a name and a color. Tags are attached to monitors with the tags argument of createMonitor / updateMonitor, which also creates a tag that does not exist yet, so this is only needed to define a tag ahead of use. Names are not unique: check listTags first to avoid a duplicate. To rename or recolor a tag use updateTag; to remove one, deleteTag.

arguments.name: name
arguments.desc: Tag name

arguments.name: color
arguments.desc: Tag color as a hex string (e.g. "#ff0000") or CSS color name

name: deleteAPIKey
description: Permanently deletes an API key: anything still using it is refused from then on. To switch it off but keep it, use setAPIKeyActive. Find the ID with listAPIKeys.

arguments.name: keyID
arguments.desc: The ID of the API key to delete

name: deleteDockerHost
description: Permanently deletes a Docker daemon connection. Monitors that referenced it are kept, but their docker_host is cleared, so they stop working until given another. Find the ID with listDockerHosts.

arguments.name: dockerHostID
arguments.desc: The ID of the docker host to delete

name: deleteIncident
description: Permanently deletes an incident from a status page and its history. To end an incident but keep its record, use resolveIncident. Find the ID with listIncidents.

arguments.name: slug
arguments.desc: The status page slug. Find slugs with listStatusPages.

arguments.name: incidentID
arguments.desc: The ID of the incident to delete

name: deleteMaintenanceWindow
description: Permanently deletes a maintenance window; its monitors return to normal alerting. To switch it off but keep it, use setMaintenanceWindowActive. Find the ID with listMaintenanceWindows.

arguments.name: maintenanceID
arguments.desc: The ID of the maintenance window to delete

name: deleteMonitor
description: Permanently deletes a monitor and all its heartbeat history. This cannot be undone. Deleting a group does not delete the monitors in it: they move to the top level. To stop checks but keep the monitor and its history, use setMonitorActive. Find the ID with listMonitors.

arguments.name: monitorID
arguments.desc: The ID of the monitor to delete

name: deleteNotification
description: Permanently deletes a notification channel. Monitors that used it stop alerting through it, and this cannot be undone. To change a channel instead, use updateNotification. Find the ID with listNotifications.

arguments.name: notificationID
arguments.desc: The ID of the notification to delete

name: deleteProxy
description: Permanently deletes a proxy. Monitors that used it are kept and send their requests directly from then on. Find the ID with listProxies.

arguments.name: proxyID
arguments.desc: The ID of the proxy to delete

name: deleteRemoteBrowser
description: Permanently deletes a remote browser. Real-browser monitors that used it are kept and fall back to the built-in Chromium. Find the ID with listRemoteBrowsers.

arguments.name: remoteBrowserID
arguments.desc: The ID of the remote browser to delete

name: deleteStatusPage
description: Permanently deletes a status page; its public URL stops working. The monitors shown on it are not affected. Find the slug with listStatusPages.

arguments.name: slug
arguments.desc: The status page slug to delete

name: deleteTag
description: Permanently deletes a tag and removes it from every monitor that carries it. An ID that does not exist still reports success. To rename or recolor a tag instead, use updateTag. Find the ID with listTags.

arguments.name: tagID
arguments.desc: The ID of the tag to delete

name: getMonitor
description: Returns one monitor's configuration by ID (check interval, notifications, tags, parent group) with its uptime and average ping. Type-specific fields such as url, hostname and port are returned only with includeTypeSpecificFields. Read it before updateMonitor. For current status use getMonitorSummary; for check history, listHeartbeats. Find IDs with listMonitors.

arguments.name: monitorID
arguments.desc: The ID of the monitor to retrieve

arguments.name: includeTypeSpecificFields
arguments.desc: Also return type-specific fields such as url, hostname and port (default: false)

arguments.name: includeSecrets
arguments.desc: Return credentials in full instead of "***"; they then stay in the transcript. Default: false, or UPTIME_KUMA_INCLUDE_SECRETS.

name: getMonitorSummary
description: START HERE for status questions ("what's down?", "how is everything doing?"). Returns the current status of every monitor (UP, DOWN, PENDING or MAINTENANCE) with its latest heartbeat message, lastBeatTime, type and tags. Filters: keywords, type, status, active, maintenance, tags, parent group. A push monitor that has stopped beating keeps its last status, so check lastBeatTime, which is UTC with no zone marker. For configuration use listMonitors; for history, listHeartbeats.

arguments.name: keywords
arguments.desc: Space-separated keywords matched against the monitor's pathName, case-insensitively; all must match

arguments.name: type
arguments.desc: Monitor type(s), comma-separated. listMonitorTypes lists them.

arguments.name: active
arguments.desc: true: only active monitors; false: only paused ones

arguments.name: maintenance
arguments.desc: true: only monitors in maintenance; false: only those not in maintenance

arguments.name: tags
arguments.desc: Tags a monitor must all have, comma-separated, each "name" or "name=value", case-insensitive. E.g. "production,env=staging"

arguments.name: parentId
arguments.desc: Only the direct children of this group monitor (not recursive); null for top-level monitors

arguments.name: status
arguments.desc: Current status, comma-separated, by name or number: down (0), up (1), pending (2), maintenance (3). E.g. "down,pending"

name: getMonitorTypeFields
description: Describes the fields one monitor type takes: which are required, which are optional, what each means and accepts, its default, and whether it is passed at the top level or inside typeFields. Call it before createMonitor, and before updateMonitor changes a type or a type-specific field: those tools do not describe these fields. Type names come from listMonitorTypes.

arguments.name: type
arguments.desc: The monitor type, e.g. http, mqtt, snmp. Use listMonitorTypes for all options.

name: getMonitorUptime
description: Returns a monitor's uptime percentage, check counts and ping (min/avg/max) over the last N hours, up to a year, with the minutes, hours or days in which checks failed, newest first. Use it for "what was the uptime this week?"; for the current status use getMonitorSummary, and for individual checks listHeartbeats. Counted as Uptime Kuma counts them: PENDING is down, and MAINTENANCE is neither.

arguments.name: monitorID
arguments.desc: The monitor to report on. Find IDs with listMonitors.

arguments.name: hours
arguments.desc: How far back, in hours (default: 24; e.g. 168 for a week, 720 for 30 days). Up to 24 is counted per minute, up to 720 per hour, beyond that per whole day.

name: getNotificationTypeFields
description: Describes the config fields one notification type takes: which are required, which are optional and what each means. Call it before createNotification, or before updateNotification changes a type or its settings: field names are case-sensitive and Uptime Kuma saves a misspelled one without complaint. The common types are covered; for the rest it says so, and their field names can be copied from an existing channel in listNotifications. Type names come from listNotificationTypes.

arguments.name: type
arguments.desc: The notification type, e.g. slack, smtp, PagerDuty. Use listNotificationTypes for all options.

name: getSettings
description: Returns the Uptime Kuma server settings, such as timezone, primary base URL and data retention. Only settings that have been saved are returned, so a missing key (for example primaryBaseURL) has never been set. Credentials read "***" unless includeSecrets is set. To change a setting use updateSettings.

arguments.name: includeSecrets
arguments.desc: Return credentials in full instead of "***"; they then stay in the transcript. Default: false, or UPTIME_KUMA_INCLUDE_SECRETS.

name: getStatusPage
description: Returns one status page by slug: its settings, its ordered groups with the monitors in each, and its active incidents. Works for unpublished pages too. Read it before updateStatusPage. Find slugs with listStatusPages.

arguments.name: slug
arguments.desc: The status page slug (the URL-safe identifier)

name: listAPIKeys
description: Returns the API keys for Uptime Kuma's API (such as its Prometheus /metrics endpoint) with name, status (active, inactive or expired) and expiry. The keys themselves cannot be read back: they are shown once, by createAPIKey.

name: listDockerHosts
description: Returns the Docker daemon connections configured in Uptime Kuma. A docker monitor refers to one by ID in its docker_host field. Credentials embedded in a dockerDaemon URL read "***" unless includeSecrets is set.

arguments.name: includeSecrets
arguments.desc: Return credentials in full instead of "***"; they then stay in the transcript. Default: false, or UPTIME_KUMA_INCLUDE_SECRETS.

name: listHeartbeats
description: Returns check history (status, response time, message), newest first, keyed by monitor ID: for one monitor when monitorID is given, otherwise for every monitor. Only the latest beat per monitor is returned unless maxHeartbeats is set (up to 100; keep it at 10 or less for one monitor and 5 or less for all, unless asked for more). important: true returns only the status changes for one monitor, which is history and not the current status. For current status use getMonitorSummary. Credentials inside a message URL read "***" unless includeSecrets is set.

arguments.name: monitorID
arguments.desc: The monitor to read. Omit for every monitor. Find IDs with listMonitors.

arguments.name: maxHeartbeats
arguments.desc: How many of the most recent beats to return per monitor, up to 100 (default: 1)

arguments.name: important
arguments.desc: Return only IMPORTANT beats — the status changes behind Uptime Kuma's event list — fetched live from the server rather than the cache. Needs monitorID. History only: the newest important beat is not the monitor's current status.

arguments.name: includeSecrets
arguments.desc: Return credentials in full instead of "***"; they then stay in the transcript. Default: false, or UPTIME_KUMA_INCLUDE_SECRETS.

name: listIncidents
description: Returns a status page's incidents, newest first, 10 per call, resolved ones included; pass nextCursor back as cursor for the next 10. An incident shows on the page while it is both pinned and active. getStatusPage also returns the ones showing now.

arguments.name: slug
arguments.desc: The status page slug. Find slugs with listStatusPages.

arguments.name: cursor
arguments.desc: nextCursor from the previous call, for the next page

name: listMaintenanceWindows
description: Returns every maintenance window with its schedule, whether it is active, monitorIDs (the monitors it suppresses) and statusPageSlugs (the status pages that announce it). A window with an empty monitorIDs list suppresses nothing. Use it to find the ID that updateMaintenanceWindow, setMaintenanceWindowActive and deleteMaintenanceWindow take.

name: listMonitors
description: Returns the configuration of every monitor, or of those matching the filters (keywords, type, active, maintenance, tags, parent group). Use it to find monitor IDs or compare settings; for current UP/DOWN status use getMonitorSummary instead. Type-specific fields such as url, hostname and port are returned only with includeTypeSpecificFields.

arguments.name: includeTypeSpecificFields
arguments.desc: Also return type-specific fields such as url, hostname and port (default: false)

arguments.name: keywords
arguments.desc: Space-separated keywords matched against the monitor's pathName, case-insensitively; all must match

arguments.name: type
arguments.desc: Monitor type(s), comma-separated. listMonitorTypes lists them.

arguments.name: active
arguments.desc: true: only active monitors; false: only paused ones

arguments.name: maintenance
arguments.desc: true: only monitors in maintenance; false: only those not in maintenance

arguments.name: tags
arguments.desc: Tags a monitor must all have, comma-separated, each "name" or "name=value", case-insensitive. E.g. "production,env=staging"

arguments.name: parentId
arguments.desc: Only the direct children of this group monitor (not recursive); null for top-level monitors

arguments.name: includeSecrets
arguments.desc: Return credentials in full instead of "***"; they then stay in the transcript. Default: false, or UPTIME_KUMA_INCLUDE_SECRETS.

name: listMonitorTypes
description: Returns every monitor type Uptime Kuma supports and what each one checks. Use it to choose the type for createMonitor (there are dedicated types for game servers, MQTT, SNMP, gRPC, Docker containers and more) and for the valid values of type filters. For the fields a type takes, call getMonitorTypeFields.

name: listNotifications
description: Returns every notification channel (Slack, ntfy, Discord, email, webhooks and so on) with its id, type and type-specific config. Credentials in config are withheld unless includeSecrets is set, and redactedConfigKeys names the withheld fields. To attach a channel to a monitor, pass its id in notificationIDList of createMonitor / updateMonitor.

arguments.name: includeSecrets
arguments.desc: Return credentials in full instead of "***"; they then stay in the transcript. Default: false, or UPTIME_KUMA_INCLUDE_SECRETS.

name: listNotificationTypes
description: Returns every notification type Uptime Kuma supports (Slack, email, ntfy, Telegram, webhooks and about a hundred more) with the exact, case-sensitive type string createNotification takes. An older Uptime Kuma may lack the newest ones. For the fields a type takes, call getNotificationTypeFields.

name: listProxies
description: Returns the proxies monitors can send their requests through, with protocol, host, port and username. An HTTP-type monitor uses one by ID in its proxyId field. Passwords read "***" unless includeSecrets is set.

arguments.name: includeSecrets
arguments.desc: Return credentials in full instead of "***"; they then stay in the transcript. Default: false, or UPTIME_KUMA_INCLUDE_SECRETS.

name: listRemoteBrowsers
description: Returns the remote browsers (a Chrome reachable over WebSocket, e.g. browserless) that real-browser monitors can run in instead of the built-in Chromium. A monitor uses one by ID in its remote_browser field. Tokens and logins in a URL read "***" unless includeSecrets is set.

arguments.name: includeSecrets
arguments.desc: Return credentials in full instead of "***"; they then stay in the transcript. Default: false, or UPTIME_KUMA_INCLUDE_SECRETS.

name: listStatusPages
description: Returns every status page with its slug, title, published state and custom domains. The list dates from login, so a page that another client or the web UI created or deleted since may be missing or still listed; changes made through this server show at once, and getStatusPage always reads fresh.

name: listTags
description: Returns every tag defined in Uptime Kuma with its ID, name and color. To see which monitors carry a tag, filter listMonitors or getMonitorSummary by tag name.

name: resolveIncident
description: Marks an incident as over: it leaves the status page but stays in listIncidents. To remove it from the history too, use deleteIncident. Find the ID with listIncidents or getStatusPage.

arguments.name: slug
arguments.desc: The status page slug. Find slugs with listStatusPages.

arguments.name: incidentID
arguments.desc: The ID of the incident to resolve

name: setAPIKeyActive
description: Switches an API key off (active: false), so requests using it are refused, or back on (active: true). An expired key stays expired. To remove it for good use deleteAPIKey. Find the ID with listAPIKeys.

arguments.name: keyID
arguments.desc: The ID of the API key

arguments.name: active
arguments.desc: false switches the key off, true back on

name: setMaintenanceWindowActive
description: Switches a maintenance window off (active: false) or back on (active: true). Off, it stops suppressing its monitors and its schedule stops; on, a manual window starts maintenance immediately and a scheduled one follows its schedule again. It acts on a maintenance window; to stop a monitor's checks use setMonitorActive. Find the ID with listMaintenanceWindows.

arguments.name: maintenanceID
arguments.desc: The ID of the maintenance window to switch

arguments.name: active
arguments.desc: false switches the window off, true switches it on

name: setMonitorActive
description: Pauses (active: false) or resumes (active: true) a monitor. A paused monitor stops checking, recording heartbeats and alerting; its configuration and history are kept, and resuming restarts checks at once. Setting the state it already has changes nothing. For planned downtime on a schedule use createMaintenanceWindow instead; setMaintenanceWindowActive acts on a maintenance window, not a monitor. Find the ID with listMonitors.

arguments.name: monitorID
arguments.desc: The ID of the monitor to pause or resume

arguments.name: active
arguments.desc: false pauses the monitor, true resumes it

name: testDockerHost
description: Tests whether Uptime Kuma can reach a Docker daemon, without saving anything. On success the message gives the number of containers. Use it before createDockerHost or updateDockerHost.

arguments.name: name
arguments.desc: Display name (used only in the test request)

arguments.name: dockerType
arguments.desc: "socket" for a unix socket path, "tcp" for an HTTP/HTTPS URL

arguments.name: dockerDaemon
arguments.desc: Unix socket path or TCP URL to probe

name: testNotification
description: Sends a test message ("<channel name> Testing") through a saved notification channel, as the Test button in Uptime Kuma does, to check its settings work. It really is delivered, to Slack, email or wherever the channel points, so do not repeat it without reason. Nothing is saved. Find the ID with listNotifications.

arguments.name: notificationID
arguments.desc: The ID of the channel to test

name: testRemoteBrowser
description: Checks that Uptime Kuma can drive a browser at a WebSocket URL, without saving anything: pass url to try one before createRemoteBrowser, or remoteBrowserID to check a saved one.

arguments.name: url
arguments.desc: A ws:// or wss:// endpoint to try

arguments.name: remoteBrowserID
arguments.desc: A saved remote browser to check

name: updateDockerHost
description: Updates an existing Docker daemon connection. Only the fields you pass change. Credentials in a dockerDaemon URL sent back as "***" keep their stored value. Check a new address with testDockerHost first. Find the ID with listDockerHosts.

arguments.name: dockerHostID
arguments.desc: The ID of the docker host to update

arguments.name: name
arguments.desc: New human-readable name

arguments.name: dockerType
arguments.desc: New connection type

arguments.name: dockerDaemon
arguments.desc: New socket path or TCP URL

name: updateIncident
description: Changes an incident banner. Only the fields you pass change. pinned: false takes it off the page without resolving it; to end an incident use resolveIncident. Find the ID with listIncidents or getStatusPage.

arguments.name: slug
arguments.desc: The status page slug. Find slugs with listStatusPages.

arguments.name: incidentID
arguments.desc: The ID of the incident to change

arguments.name: title
arguments.desc: New headline

arguments.name: content
arguments.desc: New body, in Markdown

arguments.name: style
arguments.desc: Banner color: primary (blue), info, warning (yellow), danger (red), light or dark

arguments.name: pinned
arguments.desc: false takes the banner off the page; true puts it back

name: updateMaintenanceWindow
description: Updates an existing maintenance window. Only the fields you pass change, except monitorIDs and statusPageSlugs, which each replace the whole list. To switch a window on or off use setMaintenanceWindowActive. Find the ID with listMaintenanceWindows.

arguments.name: maintenanceID
arguments.desc: The ID of the maintenance window to update

arguments.name: title
arguments.desc: Title of the maintenance window

arguments.name: strategy
arguments.desc: Scheduling strategy (see createMaintenanceWindow)

arguments.name: description
arguments.desc: Description or reason for the maintenance

arguments.name: timezone
arguments.desc: Timezone the dates and times are in (e.g. "America/New_York", "UTC"). Omit to follow the server timezone.

arguments.name: dateRange
arguments.desc: [start, end] as local times in the window's timezone, e.g. ["2026-10-08T10:00", "2026-10-08T12:00"]. Required for single; optional bounds for recurring strategies; ignored for manual.

arguments.name: timeRange
arguments.desc: Daily [{hours, minutes}, {hours, minutes}] start and end. Required for the recurring-* strategies, ignored otherwise.

arguments.name: weekdays
arguments.desc: Days of week (0=Sunday … 6=Saturday) for recurring-weekday strategy

arguments.name: daysOfMonth
arguments.desc: Days of month (1-31) for recurring-day-of-month strategy

arguments.name: intervalDay
arguments.desc: Interval in days for recurring-interval strategy

arguments.name: cron
arguments.desc: Cron expression for when the window starts, e.g. "30 3 * * *" (03:30 daily), for the cron strategy

arguments.name: durationMinutes
arguments.desc: How long each window lasts, in minutes, for the cron strategy

arguments.name: monitorIDs
arguments.desc: IDs of the monitors this window suppresses. A window with no monitors suppresses nothing. On update this REPLACES the current list; pass [] to detach all.

arguments.name: statusPageSlugs
arguments.desc: Slugs of the status pages that announce this window while it is in effect. On update this REPLACES the current list; pass [] to remove it from all. Find slugs with listStatusPages.

name: updateMonitor
description: Updates an existing monitor. Only the fields you pass change; the rest keep their stored values. Passing a different type converts the monitor in place, keeping its ID and history, and needs the new type's required fields, passed here or already stored. Type-specific fields go in typeFields: call getMonitorTypeFields for them. A credential sent back as "***" keeps its stored value. Read the current configuration with getMonitor; to only stop or restart checks use setMonitorActive.

arguments.name: monitorID
arguments.desc: The ID of the monitor to update

arguments.name: parent
arguments.desc: Parent group monitor ID — re-parents this monitor into that group. Pass null to move it to the top level.

arguments.name: description
arguments.desc: Free-text description shown on the monitor page

arguments.name: type
arguments.desc: New monitor type: converts the monitor in place. Pass the new type's required fields in the same call. A group cannot be converted.

arguments.name: resendInterval
arguments.desc: Resend notification every N checks while down (0 = disabled)

arguments.name: timeout
arguments.desc: Request timeout in seconds. Avoid 0: Uptime Kuma turns a stored 0 into a timeout of about 13 hours, so the monitor never reports DOWN.

arguments.name: jsonPath
arguments.desc: JSONata expression for json-query monitors. Must resolve to a primitive.

arguments.name: jsonPathOperator
arguments.desc: Comparison operator for json-query monitors.

arguments.name: expectedValue
arguments.desc: Threshold the json-query result is compared against, stored as a string.

arguments.name: pushToken
arguments.desc: Push token — the secret in the ping URL. Changing it invalidates the existing URL and any sender still using it stops beating.

arguments.name: name
arguments.desc: Display name

arguments.name: url
arguments.desc: URL to monitor

arguments.name: hostname
arguments.desc: Hostname

arguments.name: port
arguments.desc: Port number

arguments.name: interval
arguments.desc: Check interval in seconds (min: 1)

arguments.name: retryInterval
arguments.desc: Retry interval in seconds (min: 1)

arguments.name: maxretries
arguments.desc: Max retries before marking as down

arguments.name: notificationIDList
arguments.desc: Notification ID map

arguments.name: tags
arguments.desc: Tags to assign

arguments.name: keyword
arguments.desc: Keyword to search for

arguments.name: invertKeyword
arguments.desc: Invert keyword match

arguments.name: method
arguments.desc: HTTP method

arguments.name: body
arguments.desc: HTTP request body

arguments.name: headers
arguments.desc: HTTP headers as JSON string

arguments.name: accepted_statuscodes
arguments.desc: Accepted HTTP status codes

arguments.name: ignoreTls
arguments.desc: Ignore TLS/SSL errors

arguments.name: maxredirects
arguments.desc: Max HTTP redirects

arguments.name: upsideDown
arguments.desc: Invert status

arguments.name: expiryNotification
arguments.desc: Notify before the TLS certificate expires (http, keyword, json-query, globalping)

arguments.name: domainExpiryNotification
arguments.desc: Notify before the domain registration expires. Needs Uptime Kuma 2.1 or later.

arguments.name: active
arguments.desc: Whether the monitor is active

arguments.name: docker_container
arguments.desc: Docker container name (required for docker type)

arguments.name: docker_host
arguments.desc: Docker host ID (required for docker type). Use listDockerHosts to find available IDs.

arguments.name: dns_resolve_server
arguments.desc: DNS server to use for resolution (for dns type)

arguments.name: dns_resolve_type
arguments.desc: DNS record type to query (dns and globalping)

arguments.name: databaseConnectionString
arguments.desc: Connection string for the database monitor types. Sending "***" back keeps the stored value.

arguments.name: databaseQuery
arguments.desc: Query a database monitor runs

arguments.name: databasePassword
arguments.desc: Password for mysql monitors. Sending "***" back keeps the stored value.

arguments.name: radiusPassword
arguments.desc: The RADIUS password (radius). Sending "***" back keeps the stored value.

arguments.name: typeFields
arguments.desc: Type-specific fields, e.g. {"mqttTopic": "sensors/#"} for mqtt or {"bearer_token": "…"} for HTTP with auth. getMonitorTypeFields names them for a type; an unknown name is refused. getMonitor returns them at the top level.

name: updateNotification
description: Updates an existing notification channel. Only what you pass changes: name, isDefault and each field in config are merged onto the stored channel, so a rename keeps the credentials. A secret sent back as "***" keeps its stored value. Changing type discards the stored config, so pass the new type's full config with it. Find the ID with listNotifications; to add a channel use createNotification, and to remove one, deleteNotification.

arguments.name: notificationID
arguments.desc: The ID of the notification to update

arguments.name: name
arguments.desc: New human-readable name. Omit to keep the current one.

arguments.name: type
arguments.desc: New notification type. Omit to keep the current one. A different type discards the stored config.

arguments.name: isDefault
arguments.desc: Enable by default for new monitors. Omit to keep the current value.

arguments.name: applyExisting
arguments.desc: Attach this channel to every existing monitor now. One-off: it is not stored.

arguments.name: config
arguments.desc: Type-specific configuration fields to change. Fields left out keep their stored value, unless type changes.

name: updateProxy
description: Changes a proxy. Only the fields you pass change; a password sent back as "***" keeps the stored one. Clear username (pass "") to stop sending a login. Find the ID with listProxies.

arguments.name: proxyID
arguments.desc: The ID of the proxy to change

arguments.name: protocol
arguments.desc: New protocol: http, https, socks, socks5, socks5h, socks4

arguments.name: host
arguments.desc: New host name or IP address

arguments.name: port
arguments.desc: New port

arguments.name: username
arguments.desc: "" stops sending a login

arguments.name: password
arguments.desc: A credential: "***" keeps the stored one

arguments.name: default
arguments.desc: Make it the proxy the web UI preselects for new monitors; the previous default stops being one

arguments.name: applyExisting
arguments.desc: Also route every existing monitor through this proxy now. One-off: it is not stored.

arguments.name: includeSecrets
arguments.desc: Return credentials in full instead of "***"; they then stay in the transcript. Default: false, or UPTIME_KUMA_INCLUDE_SECRETS.

name: updateRemoteBrowser
description: Changes a remote browser's name or URL; what you leave out keeps its stored value. To change the URL pass it in full: a URL with "***" in it is refused, since it would overwrite the stored token. Find the ID with listRemoteBrowsers.

arguments.name: remoteBrowserID
arguments.desc: The ID of the remote browser to change

arguments.name: name
arguments.desc: New name

arguments.name: url
arguments.desc: New ws:// or wss:// endpoint, in full

arguments.name: includeSecrets
arguments.desc: Return credentials in full instead of "***"; they then stay in the transcript. Default: false, or UPTIME_KUMA_INCLUDE_SECRETS.

name: updateSettings
description: Changes Uptime Kuma server settings. Pass only what should change; every other setting keeps its stored value. Returns the settings as saved. Turning login off (disableAuth: true) needs currentPassword and leaves the dashboard open to anyone who can reach it. Read the current values with getSettings.

arguments.name: serverTimezone
arguments.desc: IANA timezone the server shows times and schedules maintenance in, e.g. "America/Edmonton" or "UTC"

arguments.name: primaryBaseURL
arguments.desc: The public address of this Uptime Kuma, used for links in notifications, e.g. "https://status.example.com". "" clears it.

arguments.name: entryPage
arguments.desc: What "/" opens: "dashboard", or a status page as "statusPage-<slug>". Find slugs with listStatusPages.

arguments.name: keepDataPeriodDays
arguments.desc: Days of heartbeat history to keep; older beats are deleted

arguments.name: tlsExpiryNotifyDays
arguments.desc: Days before a TLS certificate expires to send a warning, e.g. [7, 14, 21]. Replaces the whole list.

arguments.name: domainExpiryNotifyDays
arguments.desc: Days before a domain registration expires to send a warning. Replaces the whole list.

arguments.name: searchEngineIndex
arguments.desc: Let search engines index status pages

arguments.name: checkUpdate
arguments.desc: Show when a new Uptime Kuma version is available

arguments.name: trustProxy
arguments.desc: Trust X-Forwarded-* headers. Set only when Uptime Kuma sits behind a reverse proxy.

arguments.name: nscd
arguments.desc: Cache DNS lookups with NSCD (Docker images only)

arguments.name: chromeExecutable
arguments.desc: Path of the Chrome or Chromium binary real-browser monitors run, e.g. "/usr/bin/chromium". "" auto-detects. Changing it restarts the browser.

arguments.name: apiEnabled
arguments.desc: The "API" switch in Settings > General

arguments.name: prometheusApiEnabled
arguments.desc: Collect Prometheus metrics. Changing it starts or stops the collection.

arguments.name: steamAPIKey
arguments.desc: Steam Web API key, used by Steam game server monitors. A credential: "***" (what read tools return) keeps the stored key, "" clears it.

arguments.name: globalpingApiToken
arguments.desc: Globalping API token, used by globalping monitors. A credential: "***" (what read tools return) keeps the stored token, "" clears it.

arguments.name: disableAuth
arguments.desc: true turns login off: anyone who can reach Uptime Kuma gets full control. Needs currentPassword. false turns login back on and logs out every other session.

arguments.name: currentPassword
arguments.desc: The admin password. Required only to turn login off (disableAuth: true) while it is on; never stored or returned.

arguments.name: includeSecrets
arguments.desc: Return credentials in full instead of "***"; they then stay in the transcript. Default: false, or UPTIME_KUMA_INCLUDE_SECRETS.

name: updateStatusPage
description: Updates an existing status page. config holds only the settings to change; the rest keep their stored values. publicGroupList, when passed, replaces all of the page's groups: a group left out is deleted, and a group is kept rather than recreated only if you include its id. Omit it to leave the groups as they are. Read the current state with getStatusPage first.

arguments.name: slug
arguments.desc: The status page slug (immutable identifier)

arguments.name: config
arguments.desc: The settings to change, merged onto the stored page: title, description, theme, published, showTags, showPoweredBy, domainNameList, customCSS, footerText, icon, etc. Omit to change only the groups.

arguments.name: publicGroupList
arguments.desc: Ordered groups, replacing all current ones. Each: {id?, name, monitorList: [{id}]}. Omit to keep the current groups.

arguments.name: imgDataUrl
arguments.desc: Icon as data URL. Omit or pass empty string to keep existing.

name: updateTag
description: Renames or recolors an existing tag. Pass name, color or both; whichever you omit keeps its current value. The change shows on every monitor that carries the tag. Find the ID with listTags; to add a tag use createTag.

arguments.name: tagID
arguments.desc: The ID of the tag to update

arguments.name: name
arguments.desc: New tag name. Omit to keep the current one.

arguments.name: color
arguments.desc: New tag color as a hex string (e.g. "#ff0000") or CSS color name. Omit to keep the current one.
